Curriculum › Year 2

Year 2: what your child practises

In Year 2, Sharpwise has 43 topics in maths and 21 topics in English. Each one is below in plain words, with ideas to try at home.

Year 2 topics follow the National Curriculum for England. This page is made from the game's own list of topics, so it changes when the game does.

Play Sharpwise

Maths in Year 2

43 topics, grouped by the part of the curriculum each one practises.

Number: number and place value

Tens & Ones
Place value
Compare < > =
Compare to 100
Count in 2s, 3s, 5s, 10s
Count in steps
Number Words
Numbers to 100 in words
Order Up!
Order numbers to 100
Number Line
Number line, steps
Estimate the Number
Estimate numbers on a number line

Try at home:

  • Make numbers from pairs of playing cards and ask which digit stands for tens and which for ones.
  • Put two heaps of socks or coins side by side and ask which has more, and by how many.
  • Count stairs, spoons or steps together, then count backwards, and stop to ask what comes next.
  • Chalk a number line on the path and hop along it, asking where a number sits between two others.

Number: addition and subtraction

Adding to 100
2-digit addition
Subtracting
2-digit subtraction
Related Facts
Derive and use related facts up to 100
Three Numbers
Add three 1-digit
Missing Number
Inverse, missing number
Story Sums
Solve problems with addition and subtraction in context
Swap It Round
Addition and multiplication can be done in any order; subtraction and division cannot
Balance the Scales
Equivalence, inverse, tables

Try at home:

  • Add the prices of two snacks in your head, then take one away to check the answer.
  • Lay out 10 spoons and ask how many more make 10.

Number: multiplication and division

2, 5, 10 Times Tables
2, 5, 10 tables ×÷
2× table
2 times table
5× table
5 times table
10× table
10 times table
Story Times
Solve problems in contexts using the 2, 5 and 10 tables
Odd or Even
Odd and even

Try at home:

  • Set out egg boxes or muffin trays and count the rows and columns to find the lots of.

Number: fractions

Fractions
1/3 1/4 2/4 3/4
Same Fraction
Equivalence of 2/4 and 1/2

Try at home:

  • Cut a pizza or an apple into equal parts and ask for one half, one quarter or three quarters.

Measurement

Money £ and p
Money, change
Shop Stories
Money problems in a practical context, including change
Coin Combinations
Find different combinations of coins that equal the same amounts of money
Telling Time
Time to 5 min
Length: cm & m
Length (cm/m)
Mass: g & kg
Mass (g/kg)
Capacity: ml & l
Capacity (ml/l)
Compare Measures < > =
Compare measures and record using >, < and =
Temperature
Temperature (°C)
Read the Scale
Read a ruler, scale, thermometer or jug
Time & Durations
Compare and sequence intervals of time

Try at home:

  • Let your child pay with real coins at the shop and work out the change together.
  • Ask what the clock will say in half an hour, then check when the time comes.
  • Compare a cup, a jug and a bowl: which holds more? Use a ruler or shoe-lengths to measure the table.

Geometry: properties of shapes

3-D Shapes
3-D shapes — faces, edges, vertices
Shapes Around Us
Compare and sort common 3-D shapes and everyday objects
Faces of Shapes
Identify 2-D shapes on the surface of 3-D shapes
Mirror Lines
Line symmetry in a vertical line

Try at home:

  • Go on a shape hunt around the house for circles, boxes, cylinders and right angles.

Geometry: position and direction

What Comes Next?
Order and arrange objects in patterns and sequences
Turns & Right Angles
Position, direction, rotation as right angles

Try at home:

  • Count stairs, spoons or steps together, then count backwards, and stop to ask what comes next.
  • Go on a shape hunt around the house for circles, boxes, cylinders and right angles.

Statistics

Charts & Tallies
Pictograms, tally charts, block diagrams
Most to Least
Sort the categories by quantity
Read the Table
Interpret simple tables

Try at home:

  • Tally the cars passing the window or the colours of socks, then say which has most and fewest.

English in Year 2

21 topics, grouped by the part of the curriculum each one practises.

Reading: comprehension

Story Time
Listening; inference; answering questions
What Happened?
Making inferences on the basis of what is being said and done

Try at home:

  • After a bedtime story, ask who it was about, what happened and where, then how many or why.

Writing: transcription (spelling)

Tricky Words
Common exception words
Contractions don't
Contractions
Endings -ful -ly
Suffixes
Changing Endings
Suffixes that change the root (drop e, double, y→i)
Sound-alike Words
Homophones
Silent Letters
/n/ spelt kn and gn, /r/ spelt wr at the start of words
Word Endings
The /l/ or /əl/ sound spelt -le, -el, -al and -il at the end of words
Badge or Cage?
The /dʒ/ sound spelt -dge and -ge at the end of words, and g before e, i and y
City or Sity?
The /s/ sound spelt c before e, i and y
Station or Stashin?
Words ending in -tion
Walk or Wawk?
a before l, o for /ʌ/, -ey, a after w and qu, or and ar after w, s for /ʒ/

Try at home:

  • Choose three words a night: look, cover, write, check, and then say what makes each one tricky.

Writing: transcription (handwriting)

Trace Words
Handwriting

Try at home:

  • Write big letters and numbers in flour, sand or with a finger on a steamy window.

Writing: composition

Story Sentences
Word order, conjunctions, noun phrases

Try at home:

  • Read a few lines together every day and ask your child to point to the tricky words.

Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation

Naming Words
Nouns formed with -er and by compounding
Word Detective
Nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs
Sentence Types
Statements, questions, commands and exclamations
Then & Now
Present and past tense, including the progressive
Fix the Sentence
Commas, apostrophes
Joining Words
Co-ordination (and, or, but) and subordination (because, when, if, that)

Try at home:

  • Look at a favourite book together and spot the full stops, question marks and describing words.

These parts of the curriculum have no topic in this year yet.

  • Spoken language (English)
